Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Image 3 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the yard side of the primary school ZŠ Sokolíkova 2 in Dúbravka, Bratislava (opened 1974), seen from its school yard. Image 2 is a photo of the same school building from its street side: the 1970s typified school with long horizontal ribbon windows with many slim vertical mullions, horizontal wall bands between the window rows, a flat roof with a plain attic edge - paint the yard side with exactly this architecture, but NOT its grey mosaic cladding and NOT its white plastic windows: in 1995 the walls are one single plain colour, a smooth pale yellowish (light ochre-cream) render, slightly weathered, and the windows are the original 1970s ones with slim white-painted frames.

Brief: the school yard in June 1995: playground asphalt, a bench under a linden, an art panel with four shapes and a rhythmic drawing. Warm early-summer afternoon light from the left, fresh green trees, a clear sky.

Camera: standing on the yard asphalt, about 2.1 m high, looking across the school grounds at the long yard facade; vertical lines stay vertical; the horizon is at y ~380. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch:
- LEFT HALF: a red clay running track (an old school "antuka" cinder track, about four lanes wide, matt brick-red with faint white lane lines) with GRASS INSIDE IT: we see the rounded end of the oval - the track comes in from the left edge at y ~560-630, sweeps to the right in a wide curve to its turning point at x ~770, y ~495 and runs back to the left as the far straight at y ~445-455 in front of the school. Inside the curve is the grass infield. A strip of lawn lies between the track and the yard.
- RIGHT THIRD: the tall see-through fence of the playground runs straight AWAY from the camera, from the right frame edge (posts from y ~176 down to y ~685) to the far corner of the playground at x ~1228 (top y ~323, foot y ~465): dark green painted steel posts, a top rail and two thin middle rails, wire chain-link mesh you can see through, a low concrete base. It is seen from the side, as a long receding wall of mesh, NOT facing the camera. Behind the fence lies the playground: a big flat CONCRETE playground of grey concrete slabs with faded white painted lines, with basketball baskets on steel poles; at its far end a lower stretch of the same fence runs across.
- CENTRE: a narrow paved asphalt way runs along the left side of that fence from the yard straight back to the small yard entrance of the school; between the way and the track lies the lawn.
- BACKGROUND: the long three-storey main wing stands on a low grass bank across the picture, from its corner at x ~431 (roof edge y ~185, foot y ~398) to the right edge (roof edge y ~120, foot y ~404): a ground floor with a row of slim square piers and dark recessed glazing, above it two long ribbon-window floors. The yard entrance - a glazed double door with a small flat steel canopy - is at x ~997-1055 with short concrete steps down the bank to the paved way. Left of the corner stands the lower two-storey gym wing with a band of tall windows, trees beside it. Behind the school rises the wooded Dúbravka hill with a few small family houses among the trees.
- FOREGROUND: the worn grey yard asphalt from y ~640 (a low kerb at its back edge) down to the bottom edge; every yard prop stands on it with its foot at y ~640-700.

What the sketch blocks are, left to right: the gym wing, the corner of the main wing, the long yard facade with its ribbon windows and the small yard door; the clay track with the grass infield; the lawn; the paved way; the receding court fence with the concrete playground and a basketball basket behind it; on the yard: the freestanding art panel at the left in front of the track, a small grass bed with a low kerb at the back edge of the yard with the young linden growing in it, a wooden bench with concrete legs under the linden, the low red-brick service wall with a concrete coping and its inset panel of grey stones, the red water-pipe elbow at the wall's right end, a dark green steel litter bin standing by the fence at the right.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 196-396, y 436-580 of the 1920x1080 frame (10-21 % from the left, 40-54 % from the top): a freestanding painted plywood art panel on two thin steel posts at the left edge of the yard, made by pupils: four big simple shapes in bright colours along the top (a red circle, a blue triangle, a yellow square, a purple zigzag shape) and under them a rhythmic pattern - three green waves, two black strokes, six small red pieces - with no letters and no digits.
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 1560-1700, y 280-380 of the 1920x1080 frame (81-89 % from the left, 26-35 % from the top): a basketball basket at the far end of the concrete playground, seen through the fence mesh: a white backboard with a red square facing the camera, an orange hoop ring WITHOUT a net, on a grey steel pole standing on the concrete.
3. the block of the layout sketch at x 505-737, y 100-690 of the 1920x1080 frame (26-38 % from the left, 9-64 % from the top): the young linden tree in its grass bed: a thin, weak, damaged little tree - a slim slightly leaning trunk with a scraped bark scar low on the trunk, a few thin branches and a sparse crown with gaps and some yellowish leaves; it clearly struggles.
The inset stone panel of the brick wall is a grid of 3 rows x 4 columns of grey stone blocks, all in place and flush (no hole). The red pipe elbow rises from the ground and bends sideways towards the wall, ending in a flange.

Walkable floor: the band at x 0-1920, y 722-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (0-100 % from the left, 67-94 % from the top) is the worn grey asphalt of the school yard - one continuous flat surface with no kerb, no step, no edge and no change of material inside it, and nothing standing on it: no balls, no bins, no bicycles, no poles, no court lines. Only light, soft leaf shadows and old patches and cracks in the asphalt. The asphalt continues out of the left edge in front of the track (the area of the layout sketch at x 0-60, y 722-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (0-3 % from the left, 67-94 % from the top)) and out of the right edge past the near end of the fence (the area of the layout sketch at x 1860-1920, y 722-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (97-100 % from the left, 67-94 % from the top)).

Fiction rules: the bench, linden, wall, pipe, art panel, bin and baskets are game props; no real pupils or staff. 1995: no murals, no graffiti, no modern plastic windows, no satellite dishes, no artificial turf, no modern play equipment, no cars. No house numbers, no names, no school name, no signs, no logos, no lettering of any kind, no people in the windows or anywhere, no animals.

The layout sketch is a blocking aid only: paint over all of it. Do NOT draw frames, borders, outlines or boxes around objects, and keep no flat colour block. The finished picture contains no UI, no captions, no text except what is asked for above, no watermark and no people or animals unless stated above.
